title: Viewing Your First HTML File
primaryObjective: Open a local HTML file in a web browser without a server.
boundaryRationale: First-win design. The learner must see that they can control the browser immediately without theory.

title: The Anatomy of a URL
primaryObjective: Identify the scheme, domain, and path of a given URL.
boundaryRationale: Distinct cognitive model from the general request cycle.

title: How the Browser Fetches Pages
primaryObjective: Explain the URL request and response cycle, identifying the roles of the DNS, server, and browser.
boundaryRationale: Requires a separate mental model of the network vs the address itself.

title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript Roles
primaryObjective: Identify whether HTML, CSS, or JavaScript is responsible for a given structural, visual, or behavioral web feature.
boundaryRationale: Essential disambiguation before learning any syntax. Combines concept and diagnostic practice.

title: Inspecting the Web
primaryObjective: Use browser developer tools to inspect DOM elements.
boundaryRationale: Tooling boundary. Requires interactive use of the browser.

title: Modifying Live Pages
primaryObjective: Modify styles temporarily and view console output.
boundaryRationale: Practice boundary. Separates inspection from active modification.

title: The HTML Skeleton
primaryObjective: Construct a valid HTML5 document skeleton including DOCTYPE, html, head, title, and body tags.
boundaryRationale: Foundational structure needed before any content can be added.

title: Validating HTML
primaryObjective: Verify an HTML document passes W3C validation for a basic skeleton.
boundaryRationale: Debugging boundary. Teaches how to find syntax errors in the skeleton.

title: Structuring Text with Headings and Paragraphs
primaryObjective: Format text content using appropriate heading hierarchies and paragraph tags.
boundaryRationale: Semantic text content represents a distinct capability from document skeleton.

title: Linking Pages Together
primaryObjective: Connect multiple HTML documents together using anchor tags.
boundaryRationale: New capability: Interaction/navigation vs static text.

title: Navigating File Paths
primaryObjective: Construct correct relative and absolute file paths for local files.
boundaryRationale: Cognitive load boundary. Paths are abstract and require dedicated practice separate from the anchor tag syntax.

title: Structuring Lists
primaryObjective: Structure content into ordered and unordered lists.
boundaryRationale: Parent-child tag relationship practice.

title: Embedding Images
primaryObjective: Embed images using the img tag and alt attributes.
boundaryRationale: Self-closing tags and attributes are a distinct conceptual shift from lists.

title: Semantic Landmarks
primaryObjective: Build a semantically structured HTML document using header, main, article, and nav.
boundaryRationale: Conceptual shift from 'how it looks' to 'what it means'. Requires dedicated reasoning practice.

title: Building Data Tables
primaryObjective: Display tabular data using HTML table, tr, th, and td elements.
boundaryRationale: Tables require a complex nested mental model different from simple lists.

title: Creating Forms
primaryObjective: Construct a functional HTML form with varied input types.
boundaryRationale: Interactive capability shift. Inputs are the first interactive elements taught.

title: Labels and Submission
primaryObjective: Link labels to inputs and implement a submit button.
boundaryRationale: Accessibility and form state management boundary.

title: Diagnosing Accessibility Issues
primaryObjective: Identify structural accessibility violations including missing alt text and unlinked form labels.
boundaryRationale: Diagnostic boundary. Finding errors is different from writing correct code.

title: Fixing Accessibility Violations
primaryObjective: Fix common structural accessibility violations to pass a basic audit.
boundaryRationale: Application boundary. Fixing the issues identified in the audit.

title: Planning a Multi-Page Site
primaryObjective: Plan the structure and paths for a multi-page website.
boundaryRationale: Project boundary. Planning precedes implementation.

title: Building the Multi-Page Site
primaryObjective: Synthesize HTML tags, semantics, paths, and forms to build a fully linked multi-page website.
boundaryRationale: Project build boundary. Complete independent synthesis.

title: Applying Basic Styles
primaryObjective: Target specific HTML elements using type, class, and ID selectors to apply basic styling rules.
boundaryRationale: New language introduction. Focus on the selector syntax.

title: Understanding the Cascade
primaryObjective: Predict which CSS rule will apply based on specificity and the cascade.
boundaryRationale: Cognitive boundary. Specificity requires its own reasoning exercises distinct from syntax.

title: Styling Typography
primaryObjective: Style text using fonts, sizing, and weights.
boundaryRationale: Visual formatting capability.

title: Accessible Colors
primaryObjective: Apply accessible color combinations to text and backgrounds.
boundaryRationale: Accessibility boundary. Requires understanding contrast ratios.

title: The CSS Box Model
primaryObjective: Manipulate the dimensions of elements using margin, border, and padding.
boundaryRationale: Crucial mental model shift. The foundation of all layout.

title: Controlling Box Sizing
primaryObjective: Apply box-sizing to control how padding affects element width.
boundaryRationale: Nuanced control over the box model requiring dedicated practice.

title: Document Flow and Display Types
primaryObjective: Control document flow using block, inline, and inline-block.
boundaryRationale: Flow is distinct from positioning. Focuses on natural browser behavior.

title: Absolute and Relative Positioning
primaryObjective: Position elements using absolute and relative positioning.
boundaryRationale: Positioning breaks natural flow, requiring a separate mental model.

title: Introduction to Flexbox
primaryObjective: Create a flex container and align items along the main axis.
boundaryRationale: New layout system introduction.

title: Advanced Flexbox Alignment
primaryObjective: Adjust Flexbox alignment, direction, sizing, wrapping, and spacing.
boundaryRationale: Complex properties require independent practice.

title: Defining CSS Grids
primaryObjective: Construct a basic CSS Grid using templates and tracks.
boundaryRationale: New layout system. Different mental model from Flexbox.

title: Placing Grid Items
primaryObjective: Place elements within specific grid areas.
boundaryRationale: Item placement is a distinct capability from defining the grid container.

title: Media Queries
primaryObjective: Adapt layouts to different screen sizes using media queries.
boundaryRationale: Responsive capability. Requires testing across viewport sizes.

title: Fluid Units
primaryObjective: Implement fluid sizing using relative units (%, vh, vw, rem).
boundaryRationale: Distinct mathematical approach to sizing compared to static pixels.

title: Focus and Keyboard Accessibility
primaryObjective: Ensure interfaces remain usable by maintaining focus outlines.
boundaryRationale: Accessibility focus. Requires testing via keyboard navigation.

title: Planning the Responsive Interface
primaryObjective: Plan the layout transitions for a responsive webpage design.
boundaryRationale: Project boundary. Planning precedes implementation.

title: Building the Responsive Interface
primaryObjective: Synthesize selectors, box model, layout, and queries to transform a design brief into a responsive webpage.
boundaryRationale: Project build boundary. Complete independent synthesis.

title: Thinking Like a Programmer
primaryObjective: Translate a human-readable problem into a logical sequence of discrete steps (pseudocode).
boundaryRationale: Crucial shift to algorithmic thinking before learning any syntax.

title: Variables and Data Types
primaryObjective: Store, retrieve, and update data in memory using variables and identify basic data types.
boundaryRationale: Foundational programming syntax and memory management.

title: Using Operators
primaryObjective: Evaluate and manipulate data using mathematical, string, and comparison operators.
boundaryRationale: Expressions and logic are distinct from simple variable storage.

title: Writing Conditionals
primaryObjective: Control program flow by executing different code paths using if/else statements.
boundaryRationale: Branching logic introduces non-linear execution.

title: Complex Logic
primaryObjective: Combine multiple conditions using logical AND/OR operators.
boundaryRationale: Boolean logic boundary. Requires dedicated logical reasoning.

title: Writing Loops
primaryObjective: Automate repetitive tasks by writing loops that iterate until a specific condition is met.
boundaryRationale: Iteration is a major cognitive shift in programming.

title: Tracing Loops
primaryObjective: Trace the execution of a loop step-by-step to predict its final output.
boundaryRationale: Diagnostic boundary. Reading and predicting loop state is distinct from writing one.

title: Defining Functions
primaryObjective: Define and invoke JavaScript functions with parameters.
boundaryRationale: Abstraction capability. Encapsulating logic.

title: Return Values and Scope
primaryObjective: Manage function return values and identify variable scope.
boundaryRationale: Scope and return values represent complex data flow requiring dedicated focus.

title: Working with Arrays
primaryObjective: Store collections of data using arrays and access elements by index.
boundaryRationale: Data structure capability.

title: Iterating Arrays
primaryObjective: Safely iterate over arrays to transform or filter data.
boundaryRationale: Combining loops and arrays is a fundamental programming pattern.

title: Creating Objects
primaryObjective: Model complex entities using JavaScript objects with key-value pairs.
boundaryRationale: Key-value data structures require a different mental model from indexed arrays.

title: Nested Data Structures
primaryObjective: Safely access properties within nested objects and arrays of objects.
boundaryRationale: Complex traversal is a high-cognitive-load task common in real development.

title: The Debugging Process
primaryObjective: Systematically reproduce, isolate, and diagnose JavaScript errors.
boundaryRationale: Process boundary. Teaches the methodology of debugging.

title: Fixing Common Errors
primaryObjective: Fix isolated errors and verify the solution using developer tools.
boundaryRationale: Application boundary. Independent resolution of varied bugs.

title: Selecting DOM Elements
primaryObjective: Select HTML elements using JavaScript.
boundaryRationale: The bridge between logic and presentation.

title: Modifying the DOM
primaryObjective: Modify the text, styles, and classes of selected DOM elements.
boundaryRationale: Mutation boundary. Changing state versus just reading it.

title: Handling Events
primaryObjective: Attach event listeners to UI elements to respond to user interactions.
boundaryRationale: Asynchronous interaction capability.

title: Managing Form State
primaryObjective: Capture and process form submissions dynamically without page reloads.
boundaryRationale: Specific, complex event pattern crucial for web apps.

title: Using LocalStorage
primaryObjective: Save and retrieve simple data strings using the browser's LocalStorage API.
boundaryRationale: Persistence capability. First introduction to state surviving a refresh.

title: JSON Serialization
primaryObjective: Convert objects and arrays to JSON for storage and parse them upon retrieval.
boundaryRationale: Serialization boundary. Required for storing real application state.

title: Understanding Promises and Async
primaryObjective: Explain the concept of asynchronous execution and Promises.
boundaryRationale: High cognitive load topic requiring dedicated conceptual foundation.

title: Fetching API Data
primaryObjective: Fetch data from a third-party REST API and handle the JSON response.
boundaryRationale: Network capability. Getting data into the app.

title: Handling API Errors
primaryObjective: Implement error handling for failed network requests.
boundaryRationale: Reliability boundary. Managing the unhappy path.

title: Planning the Weather Dashboard
primaryObjective: Plan the state, events, and API calls for a dynamic weather app.
boundaryRationale: Project boundary. Planning an integrated app.

title: Building the Weather Dashboard
primaryObjective: Synthesize DOM manipulation, events, state, and the Fetch API to build a fully interactive application.
boundaryRationale: Project build boundary. Complete independent synthesis of JS.

title: Initializing a Repository
primaryObjective: Initialize a local Git repository.
boundaryRationale: Tooling introduction.

title: Staging and Committing
primaryObjective: Stage changes and create meaningful commits with descriptive messages.
boundaryRationale: The core Git workflow cycle.

title: Viewing History
primaryObjective: View commit history and inspect repository status.
boundaryRationale: Observability capability.

title: Recovering from Mistakes
primaryObjective: Discard uncommitted changes and unstage files safely.
boundaryRationale: Recovery boundary. Building confidence to experiment.

title: Working with Branches
primaryObjective: Create, switch between, and manage Git branches.
boundaryRationale: Branching mental model shift.

title: Connecting to GitHub
primaryObjective: Push local commits to a remote GitHub repository.
boundaryRationale: Remote networking capability.

title: Merging Branches
primaryObjective: Merge a feature branch into the main branch locally.
boundaryRationale: Integration capability.

title: Resolving Conflicts
primaryObjective: Identify and resolve simple merge conflicts.
boundaryRationale: Conflict resolution is a high cognitive load, critical debugging skill.

title: Opening and Reviewing a Pull Request
primaryObjective: Open, review, and merge a Pull Request on GitHub.
boundaryRationale: Communication capability. Essential for project portfolios.

title: Defining the Capstone Problem
primaryObjective: Define a clear, solvable problem and identify the target audience for the capstone project.
boundaryRationale: Complete independence on requirements gathering.

title: Designing the Solution
primaryObjective: Draft a technical plan including UI mockups, state shape, and component structure.
boundaryRationale: Architecture boundary before coding.

title: Building the Interface
primaryObjective: Implement the planned responsive HTML/CSS structure.
boundaryRationale: Visual build boundary.

title: Implementing Logic and State
primaryObjective: Implement JavaScript logic, event handling, and data fetching for the capstone.
boundaryRationale: Behavioral build boundary.

title: Quality Assurance and Accessibility
primaryObjective: Audit the completed capstone for bugs, responsive flaws, and accessibility violations, and resolve them.
boundaryRationale: QA boundary. Dedicated focus on quality over feature addition.

title: Finalizing Version Control
primaryObjective: Finalize the GitHub repository with clean commit history and comprehensive documentation.
boundaryRationale: Publishing boundary.

title: Presenting the Capstone
primaryObjective: Deploy the project live and write a reflective summary of technical decisions.
boundaryRationale: Final reflection and deployment.
